Based on the healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that future doctors in Lebanon may not always be applying the rules of prevention when it comes to health habits and vaccination status. The completed prompts suggest that there are various challenges and factors contributing to this issue.

In terms of physical activity and eating habits, Lebanese residents often lack a healthy lifestyle, which can lead to poor vaccination rates. Similarly, inadequate vaccination has been reported in Lebanon, highlighting the need for improved vaccination practices.

The completed prompts also mention that interventions should be implemented to promote healthy lifestyles and improve vaccination status. This suggests that future doctors may need guidance on how to design effective prevention programs tailored to Lebanese residents' unique needs.

Furthermore, the data from the completed prompts indicate that there are factors that contribute to racial and ethnic disparities in adult influenza vaccination, such as alcohol and drug use among young men. These findings emphasize the importance of addressing these underlying issues to improve vaccine uptake and reduce disparities.

Overall, it seems that future doctors in Lebanon may face challenges in applying the rules of prevention when it comes to health habits and vaccination status due to various factors such as lack of healthy lifestyles, inadequate vaccination, and racial and ethnic disparities.
